text:
maya: FYI customer on Dedicated pool reported spikes of 429s and intermittent auth failures since yesterday evening. latency also jumped to 700ms median for short requests.

maya: repro steps from customer: simple chat request hitting /v1/generate on our dedicated endpoint (pool id rp-3342). they say it started after a key rotation they did on their side.

customer: we rotated API key, then ~10% of requests started getting 401s, others get 429s. headers attached.

customer: response headers: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-limit: 60000
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 165
x-rw-request-id: rq_abc123
```

and an example 401: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"
x-rw-request-id: rq_def456
```

maya: sounds like two issues: auth blips (401) causing retries which then push them over their reserved pool burst window -> 429s. need to confirm if our auth gateway was flapping or if the rotation produced a mix of old/new tokens in flight.

sahil: can you paste the customer-id and pool id? I'll check token validation logs and LB traces. Also which region?

maya: customer id 9876, pool rp-3342, region us-west2.

ops-bot: env-sync job completed for region us-west2 at 2026-03-16T22:12:08Z (deploy id d-77). No rollback events.

jessie: quick mitigation: activate temporary burst allowance on rp-3342 and enable fallback-routing to hosted for small tokens to avoid blocking production traffic. we can do a 10m window to buy time.

sahil: checking auth logs now — seeing a handful of token validation failures exactly at 22:09-22:14Z for customer 9876. IP range shows requests coming from their new CI runner after rotation. token validation service returned 500 for ~30s due to a downstream cache miss on our side. that likely caused some clients to retry aggressively.

sahil: also looking at rate limiter metrics: the reserved pool had smoothing window set to 60s with burst budget 15000 tokens. their traffic pattern of retries pushed remaining to 0 and then queued -> 429.

maya: repro command we ran from our side to simulate (using their new token):

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}' \
  https://dedicated.us-west2.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

maya: running that in a tight loop with intermittent 500 from auth reproduces 401/429 mix.

jessie: proposed next steps: 
- short term: increase smoothing window to 120s and add +20% temporary burst headroom to rp-3342.
- medium term: add exponential backoff for client-side retries (we should add to support guidance) and make token rotation guidance explicit.
- infra: add a defensive cache warm path for the token validator so single cache miss doesn't cause 5xx flaps.

sahil: I'm going to open infra ticket to investigate cache backend error and add tracing for token validation latencies. created internal issue INF-4231.

maya: for the customer: asked them to hold off heavy retries and to stagger rollout of new key. offered to enable temporary headroom now. they're ok with fallbacks to hosted for 15 mins.

customer: thanks, enabling fallback helped. latency back to ~120ms and 429s stopped. we'll coordinate a staggered rotation tomorrow.

jessie: I'll schedule the temporary bump now (10m). maya pls confirm when you want me to remove it.

maya: remove after 30m and ping ops channel. also send customer short writeup on rotation best practices.

sahil: collected logs + traces and attached rq ids: rq_abc123, rq_def456, rq_ghi789. will link INF-4231 to this thread.

maya: thanks team. follow-ups: ops ticket for smoothing config review, infra ticket INF-4231 for token validator cache, and a KB note for customers about rotation/retry behavior.

ops-bot: note: created support follow-up ticket SPT-9988 for customer 9876 (assign to maya).
